source.title: Revisiting the Othello World Model Hypothesis

record.tranche_reason: The study tests cross-model representation alignment using supervised and unsupervised linear mapping and aligned-feature cosine similarity, rather than testing convergence as a function of scale.
record.gate_note: The reported Othello move-generation accuracy and scaling results are not rows: they do not measure representation alignment or relate alignment to model scale or capability. Table 3 reports each model pair, dataset, and mapping condition separately; these alignment results are recorded below.
record.test_reason: The study aligns final-layer representations of independently trained, architecturally different models (GPT-2, Bart, T5, Mistral, LLaMA-2, Qwen2.5) trained on the same Othello data. It uses supervised Procrustes and unsupervised adversarial-plus-Procrustes linear maps and reports post-map cosine similarity. That bears directly on V4, including the without-paired-data part, and partly on V6 through its dataset and mapping variation. It does not test convergence as a function of scale.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that seven LMs trained on Othello move sequences learn to play and induce the board layout, with near-perfect 1-hop accuracy given enough data. They report high similarity of learned board features under linear alignment, and latent move projections showing spatial structure. They take this as stronger evidence for the Othello World Model Hypothesis. In Appendix I they further claim the models converge on universal representations regardless of architecture or scale.
record.recipe_differences: Uses supervised Procrustes mapping and unsupervised adversarial/iterative-Procrustes mapping with aligned-feature cosine similarity, rather than the probing approach described for earlier Othello studies. The paper does not report a scale sweep of representation alignment.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported alignment scores differ across the CHAMPIONSHIP and SYNTHETIC datasets and between supervised and unsupervised mapping.
record.problems: Alignment is measured only after a learned mapping, with cosine similarity; no uncertainty estimates are reported. The comparison uses models trained on the same Othello task and does not test whether alignment rises with model scale or capability, whether it generalizes to other modalities, or whether it depends on other reasonable similarity measures or out-of-distribution inputs.

untested.parts: No analysis of alignment versus model size or capability. Pairs mix sizes (GPT-2-small to 7B) but no trend is computed. All models share the same data and objective, so independence of data is not tested.
No vision or language paired data, and no cross-modal models.
No downstream interchangeability: stitching, or task performance after mapping. No relative representations. No mapping of models trained on different data.
No neuron, SAE or circuit-level feature matching.
No alternative similarity metrics (CKA, mutual k-NN), neighbour settings or out-of-distribution inputs.
Shared training data and task are held constant, so their causal role is not assessed. No plateau analysis, and without a baseline the completeness of alignment cannot be judged.

missing.what: Layer-wise GPT-2-small vs Flan-T5-Base mapping similarity heatmaps, unsupervised and supervised, on 20k SYNTHETIC. Similarity ranges about 0.5–0.9 (unsupervised) and 0.6–0.8 (supervised), highest in upper layers and near the diagonal. This bears on layer dependence of alignment.
PCA visualization of 60-step representations across models in one game. It is qualitative and offered as similar trajectories across models.

record.verdict_notes: The 'regardless of scale' claim in Appendix I is asserted, not tested: there is no alignment-vs-size analysis, so V1 stays untested. Footnote 5 says all aligned models are non-pretrained and trained on 20k games. Yet Appendix C says LLaMA-2 and Mistral are tuned only through LoRA adapters, which is inconsistent with being non-pretrained; the training status of the 7B models is unclear. Similarity is cosine after an optimized Procrustes map, with no random-model or shuffled control, so absolute values may be inflated. The Othello accuracy and scale results (Tables 1–2, Figs 2–3, 7–8) are correctly excluded as rows.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test whether representation alignment rises as models become larger or more capable, or compare alignment systematically across scale and performance.
No vision-language models or paired images and captions are studied.
Does not compare models of the same architecture trained from different initializations or test shared features/subspaces across seeds.

Tests a learned linear mapping and aligned-feature cosine similarity between Othello-trained models. It does not test downstream interchangeability, stitching, relative representations, or mapping without paired data in the general settings named by the version.
Does not identify recurring interpretable neurons, SAE features, or circuits.
Reports differences across two datasets and supervised versus unsupervised mapping, but does not compare other similarity metrics, neighbour settings, or out-of-distribution inputs.

All compared models are trained for the same Othello task; the study does not vary shared training data or objectives to determine their causal role, nor assess a plateau or completeness of alignment.
